docs.title: function get_birth_vXYZ
docs.text:
std::array< double, 3 > Slots::get_birth_vXYZ (
    const Background::Background & bkg,
    const Options::Options & opts,
    const double t,
    const double x,
    const double y,
    const double z,
    const int tidx,
    const int xidx,
    const int yidx,
    const int zidx,
    pcg32 & rng
)

Picks the starting Cartesian velocity of a new particle.

For the test backgrounds (bkg_source = "test") the velocity is fixed by the test case: 10,000 m/s in Y for the gyrate, ExB, grad-B and polarization tests, 30,000 m/s along the field line (in the X-Y plane, at angle z) for the curvature test, and at rest for the friction test.

Otherwise each component is sampled from a Maxwellian with zero mean and sigma = sqrt(kT/m), giving an isotropic velocity distribution. The temperature is imp_temp_start_val if imp_temp_start_opt is "single_value", or the main ion temperature in the particle's cell if it is "ti". The ion temperature is the cell value, not interpolated.

Parameters:

  • bkg Background plasma, used for the ion temperature.
  • opts Simulation options.
  • t Starting time of the particle (s). Currently unused.
  • x Starting computational x coordinate. Currently unused.
  • y Starting computational y coordinate. Currently unused.
  • z Starting computational z coordinate. Only used by the curvature test, where z is the toroidal angle.
  • tidx Index of the nearest background time frame.
  • xidx x index of the grid cell containing the particle.
  • yidx y index of the grid cell containing the particle.
  • zidx z index of the grid cell containing the particle.
  • rng Random number generator for this thread.

Returns:

Starting velocity {vX, vY, vZ} in Cartesian space (m/s).

docs.title: function get_birth_val
docs.text:
double Slots::get_birth_val (
    const int start_opt_int,
    const double start_val,
    const double range_min,
    const double range_max,
    const double bkg_min,
    const double bkg_max,
    pcg32 & rng
)

Picks the starting value of t, x, y or z for a new particle based on the input options.

The same function is used for each coordinate, with the matching imp_*start_opt option deciding where the particle starts: 0: At start_val. 1: Uniformly random between range_min and range_max. 2: Uniformly random over the full simulation volume, between bkg_min and bkg_max. Any other value returns 0.

Parameters:

  • start_opt_int Control integer of the imp_*start_opt option.
  • start_val Starting value used when start_opt_int is 0.
  • range_min Lower end of the range used when start_opt_int is 1.
  • range_max Upper end of the range used when start_opt_int is 1.
  • bkg_min Minimum of the simulation volume, used when start_opt_int is 2.
  • bkg_max Maximum of the simulation volume, used when start_opt_int is 2.
  • rng Random number generator for this thread.

Returns:

Starting value of the coordinate.

docs.title: function make_new_particle
docs.text:
ParticleInit Slots::make_new_particle (
    const Background::Background & bkg,
    const Options::Options & opts,
    pcg32 & rng
)

Creates a new particle at its starting time, location and velocity.

The starting t, x, y and z come from get_birth_val using the imp_*start_opt options. The time index and grid cell indices are then found, the same as in impurity_transport.cpp, and the Cartesian velocity comes from get_birth_vXYZ. The computational velocity is set to zero, since it gets set on the first call to Boris::update_velocity. The weight is 1 / imp_num and the charge is imp_init_charge.

Parameters:

  • bkg Background plasma.
  • opts Simulation options.
  • rng Random number generator for this thread.

Returns:

The new particle.

explicit Slots::Slots::Slots (
    int N
)

Creates a Slots object with room for N particles.

Every per-particle vector is resized to N. The values are zero initialized, so every slot starts with state 0 (alive). The mass and atomic number are not set here, use set_mass and set_Z.

Parameters:

  • N Number of particle slots.

docs.title: function to_device
docs.text:
SlotsDevice Slots::Slots::to_device (
    int device_id=0
)

Allocates GPU memory for the particles and copies them to the device.

I think this should probably be moved to slots.cu...

The per-particle arrays are allocated and copied, except pt and iters, which are not stored on the device. The work arrays used by the GPU kernels (all_dead, counter, alive, num_dead and dead_indices) are also allocated, and all_dead is initialized to false. If GPU support was not compiled in, an error is printed and an empty SlotsDevice is returned.

Parameters:

  • device_id ID of the GPU to allocate the memory on.

Returns:

SlotsDevice struct holding the device pointers. The memory must be released with free_slots.

docs.title: function to_host
docs.text:
Slots Slots::Slots::to_host (
    const SlotsDevice & slots_d
)

Copies the particles from the device back into a new host Slots object.

The mass and the per-particle arrays on the device are copied back. pt, iters and the atomic number are not stored on the device, so they are left at zero in the returned object. The device memory is not freed, use free_slots for that. If GPU support was not compiled in, only N and the mass are set.

Parameters:

  • slots_d SlotsDevice struct returned by to_device.

Returns:

Host Slots object holding a copy of the device data.

docs.title: function bilinear_interp
docs.text:
template<typename T>
inline T Utilities::bilinear_interp (
    const T *__restrict__ table,
    const T *__restrict__ x_grid,
    int nx,
    const T *__restrict__ y_grid,
    int ny,
    T x,
    T y
)

Performs bilinear interpolation on a flattened two-dimensional lookup table stored in device memory.

The function locates the grid cell that contains the point (x, y), computes the interpolation weights in each dimension, and returns the bilinearly interpolated value. Interpolation weights are clamped to the range [0, 1] to prevent extrapolation beyond the boundaries of the tabulated data.

The table is assumed to be stored in row-major order with dimensions nx × ny, where the flattened index corresponding to (ix, iy) is ix * ny + iy.

Template parameters:

  • T Floating-point data type used for the table and coordinate arrays.

Parameters:

  • table Flattened two-dimensional lookup table of size nx * ny.
  • x_grid Monotonically increasing x-coordinate array of length nx.
  • nx Number of x-grid points.
  • y_grid Monotonically increasing y-coordinate array of length ny.
  • ny Number of y-grid points.
  • x X-coordinate at which to evaluate the table.
  • y Y-coordinate at which to evaluate the table.

Returns:

Bilinearly interpolated value at (x, y).

double Utilities::bilinear_interpolate (
    const double x0,
    const double y0,
    const double x1,
    const double y1,
    const double z00,
    const double z10,
    const double z01,
    const double z11,
    const double x,
    const double y

Performs bilinear interpolation within a rectangular region in two-dimensional (x, y) space.

The function interpolates a value at the coordinates (x, y) using values defined at the corners of a rectangle bounded by (x0, y0) and (x1, y1).

Parameters:

  • x0 Lower x-coordinate of the rectangle.
  • y0 Lower y-coordinate of the rectangle.
  • z0 Value at the lower corner.
  • x1 Upper x-coordinate of the rectangle.
  • y1 Upper y-coordinate of the rectangle.
  • z1 Value at the upper corner.
  • x X-coordinate at which to evaluate the interpolated value.
  • y Y-coordinate at which to evaluate the interpolated value.

Returns:

Bilinearly interpolated value at (x, y). Performs bilinear interpolation within a rectangular region in two-dimensional (x, y) space.

std::pair< int, int > Utilities::bracket_indices (
    const std::vector< double > & x,
    double x0
)

Finds the indices of the two grid points that bracket a specified coordinate value.

For values within the coordinate range, the returned indices correspond to the nearest lower and upper grid points that surround x0. For values outside the coordinate range, the first or last valid interval is returned so that interpolation can proceed without accessing elements beyond the array bounds.

The input coordinate array is assumed to be sorted in ascending order.

Parameters:

  • x Sorted coordinate array.
  • x0 Coordinate value for which bracketing indices are sought.

Returns:

Pair containing the lower and upper bracketing indices {lo, hi}.

docs.title: function get_neighbor_index
docs.text:
template<typename T>
int Utilities::get_neighbor_index (
    const double val,
    const std::vector< T > & cell_centers,
    const int idx
)

Returns the index of the nearest neighboring cell center to a specified cell center index.

The neighbor is selected based on which side of the cell center the value lies. If the value is greater than the cell center, the neighboring index to the right is returned. If the value is less than or equal to the cell center, the neighboring index to the left is returned.

At the edges of the grid, where only one neighboring cell exists, that neighbor is returned regardless of which side of the cell center the value lies on.

Template parameters:

  • T Data type of the cell center coordinates.

Parameters:

  • val Coordinate value of interest.
  • cell_centers Array of cell center coordinates.
  • idx Index of the reference cell center.

Returns:

Index of the neighboring cell center closest to the side of the cell containing val.

docs.text:
inline double Utilities::trilinear_interpolate (
    const double x0,
    const double y0,
    const double z0,
    const double x1,
    const double y1,
    const double z1,
    const double v000,
    const double v100,
    const double v010,
    const double v110,
    const double v001,
    const double v101,
    const double v011,
    const double v111,
    const double x,
    const double y,
    const double z
)

Performs trilinear interpolation within a rectangular cell in (x, y, z) space.

The cell is defined by the coordinates (x0, y0, z0) and (x1, y1, z1), with values specified at each of the eight cell corners. Interpolation weights are clamped to the range [0, 1] to prevent extrapolation beyond the cell boundaries. As a result, points outside the cell return the value on the nearest cell face, edge, or corner.

Corner indexing follows the usual convention:

v000 : (x0, y0, z0) v100 : (x1, y0, z0) v010 : (x0, y1, z0) v110 : (x1, y1, z0) v001 : (x0, y0, z1) v101 : (x1, y0, z1) v011 : (x0, y1, z1) v111 : (x1, y1, z1)

Parameters:

  • x0 Lower x-coordinate of the cell.
  • y0 Lower y-coordinate of the cell.
  • z0 Lower z-coordinate of the cell.
  • x1 Upper x-coordinate of the cell.
  • y1 Upper y-coordinate of the cell.
  • z1 Upper z-coordinate of the cell.

  • v100 Field value at (x1, y0, z0).
  • v010 Field value at (x0, y1, z0).
  • v110 Field value at (x1, y1, z0).
  • v001 Field value at (x0, y0, z1).
  • v101 Field value at (x1, y0, z1).
  • v011 Field value at (x0, y1, z1).
  • v111 Field value at (x1, y1, z1).
  • x X-coordinate at which to evaluate the field.
  • y Y-coordinate at which to evaluate the field.
  • z Z-coordinate at which to evaluate the field.

Interpolated field value.

docs.title: typedef BkgFPType
docs.text:
Floating point type used in most of the simulation. 

using BkgFPType =  double;

This determines the precision used in the vectors within Background and Statistics classes. This is just to reduce memory overhead, since a Statistics object is copied for each thread, so the memory can balloon quickly. Only double and float are valid, but others could be added if there is a good reason.

docs.title: typedef Inputs
docs.text:

using Inputs =  std::map<std::string, std::variant<int, double, std::string, 
    Mapc2p_ptr>>;

Define type alias for input option map. Options are either an int, double or string. This is essentially a python dictionary if you are familiar with those.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
The Gkeyll data is read through read_gkyl.py, a python interface to postgkyl, which saves each dataset to a binary file named bkg_from_pgkyl_*.bin along with a few .csv files holding the times, grid and interpolation settings. These files are then read in here. If a file already exists from a previous run it is loaded directly instead of calling read_gkyl.py again, so delete the files to regenerate the background.

docs.title: Namespaces
docs.text: Type Name namespace Slots

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
A Slots object holds a fixed number of particle "slots". Each slot holds one particle that is followed until it dies, at which point the slot is refilled with a new particle by fill_slots_cpu (or its CUDA version) until the requested number of particles has been followed. The reason for this layout is to enable a structure of arrays (SoA) memeory layout, which is more efficient memory-wise.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
This file contains some simple implementations of multidimensional vectors. Instead of storing them as actual multidimensional vectors, they are stored as flatten vectors and then () is overloaded to act as indexing.

The bottom of this file includes instatiations of Vector3D and Vector4D for the different types needed (e.g., int, double, ...). This is a pecularity needed when splitting the declarations and definitions between a header and source file, needed so the linker can find the classes for each template type.
